Playbook.name: Windows — Scheduled Task Definition File Created or Modified - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A scheduled-task definition file was created/modified under System32\Tasks (FIM; patched from the buggy substring rule that matched TpmTasks.dll). Triage: a legitimate task, or scheduled-task persistence?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A scheduled-task definition file dropped directly is a persistence mechanism (sometimes bypassing 4698 logging).

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows FIM (verified live; monitors Windows system paths). Fields: file.path, file.name, file.extension, event.action, host.name.

Signal.Name: Scheduled Task Definition File Created o

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host where the task file changed.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the scheduled-task file is a legitimate task or persistence.

Step.name: The task definition file change
Step.Purpose: The task file path/name and whether it corresponds to a known task separate benign from persistence.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fim.event-* | WHERE event.dataset == "fim.event" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND event.action IN ("created","updated") AND file.path RLIKE "(?i).*system32.*tasks.*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.action, file.path, file.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A task file with a random/unusual name, or created outside a software install, is persistence. A vendor/OS task file under a known update is benign. Correlate with 4698 (task created) and inspect the task action on the host.

Step.name: Correlate with a 4698 scheduled-task-created event
Step.Purpose: A matching 4698 gives the task's action/command for assessment; its absence (file dropped directly) is itself suspicious.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code == "4698" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, winlog.event_data.TaskName, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A matching 4698 shows who created the task and its name (pivot to PB-WIN-013 for suspicious action content). A task FILE created with NO corresponding 4698 suggests a direct-drop persistence bypassing the API - suspicious.

Node.Condition: A task file with a random name / no corresponding 4698 (direct-drop persistence), or a suspicious task action.
A vendor/OS task file created by a known software install/update.
A task file change with unclear provenance.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-FIM-TASKFILE, INV-02-FIM-TASK4698 to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the task; close as false_positive.
Remove the task; isolate if warranted; open IR; hunt the same task estate-wide.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Inspect the task action on the host; correlate with 4698.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Remove the task; open IR; hunt the same task on peers.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Restrict task creation; alert on task-file changes; correlate FIM with 4698.

QualityChecks.Check: Patched from the substring bug (matched TpmTasks.dll); now scoped to the Tasks folder. Pairs with PB-WIN-013.
